Question ID: SPEECH_U02_L02_GuidedPractice_Q01

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.02

Which statement is the best purpose for an informative speech?

answer.text: A. To confuse the audience with as many facts as possible.

feedback.text: This is not informative communication. Information should be selected and organized so the audience understands.

answer.text: B. To explain a topic clearly so the audience understands it better.

feedback.text: Correct. Informative speaking focuses on clear explanation and understanding.

answer.text: C. To entertain without teaching anything.

feedback.text: Entertainment may help delivery, but an informative speech must teach or explain.

answer.text: D. To argue a personal opinion without support.

feedback.text: That describes weak persuasion, not informative speech development.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U02_L02_GuidedPractice_Q02

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.RES.02

Which sentence best explains reasoning after evidence?

answer.text: A. This evidence is here because I found it.

feedback.text: This does not explain how the evidence supports the point.

answer.text: B. Evidence is always correct.

feedback.text: Evidence still needs to be connected to the point through reasoning.

answer.text: C. I will now move to another topic.

feedback.text: This is a transition, not reasoning.

answer.text: D. This example matters because it shows how planning makes deadlines easier to see.

feedback.text: Correct. The sentence explains why the evidence supports the point.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U02_L02_GuidedPractice_Q03

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.02

Which transition is most purposeful in an informative speech about study habits?

answer.text: A. After explaining how a planner organizes deadlines, the next step is to examine how review time supports memory.

feedback.text: Correct. This transition shows the connection between two study-habit ideas.

answer.text: B. Anyway, here is another thing.

feedback.text: This does not show how the ideas connect.

answer.text: C. My next idea is different and unrelated.

feedback.text: This tells the audience the speech is losing organization.

answer.text: D. I am done with that, so now this.

feedback.text: This is vague and does not guide the audience clearly.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U02_L02_GuidedPractice_Q04

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.SPK.01

Which speech point best supports the focus "Organized notes help students study"?

answer.text: A. Some notebooks have colorful covers.

feedback.text: This detail may be true, but it does not explain how organized notes help studying.

answer.text: B. Students sometimes carry backpacks.

feedback.text: This is related to school but not to organized notes and studying.

answer.text: C. Headings help students find important sections quickly.

feedback.text: Correct. This point directly supports how organized notes help students study.

answer.text: D. School calendars include holidays.

feedback.text: This is unrelated to organized notes.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U02_L02_GuidedPractice_Q05

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.RES.02

Which evidence best supports the point "Rehearsal improves speech timing"?

answer.text: A. A speaker who practices can notice if a section takes too long.

feedback.text: Correct. This evidence directly connects rehearsal to timing.

answer.text: B. Many students like group projects.

feedback.text: This does not support the point about rehearsal and timing.

answer.text: C. Some speeches happen in classrooms.

feedback.text: This is too general and does not prove rehearsal improves timing.

answer.text: D. Posters can be colorful.

feedback.text: This is unrelated to speech rehearsal.
